description:
📝 Notes
Mar 4, 2026
R&D daily sprint
Invited Amir Houieh Unbody io Noémi Biró Gabor Kerekes
Attachments R&D daily sprint 
Meeting records Transcript 
Summary
Gabor Kerekes provided an update on sandboxing solutions, sharing that they settled on a Mac OS solution to accelerate development, and demonstrated a Mycelium prototype in a sandbox that successfully processed a URL and linked it to existing user information. Melissa is leading a continuous research module on safety regulations throughout March, while the team is shifting focus away from the chat function toward personalized features like a bookmarking prototype, with Amir Houieh planning to continue prototyping scenarios at the UI level and connect their "brain nexus" to the Mycelium use cases for validation. Noémi Biró presented a deep dive into the safety architecture, including a six-layer message processing system with a tier classifier, and suggested that a session manager focused on user retention should be an early feature.
Details
Update on March Planning and Safety Regulations: A call with Melissa was held to discuss the March planning, specifically the stylized version of the plan, and to review their perspective on safety regulations. The safety regulations component will be a continuous research module throughout the month, led by Melissa, who will gather research material that may influence the later design of the chat function (00:01:50). It was noted that this research module is focused strictly on gathering information and understanding boundaries rather than implementation (00:03:05).
Steering Away from Chat Function: The team is shifting the focus of modules away from the chat component, which is viewed as an interesting design constraint that allows for exploration of personalized features, such as a bookmarking prototype. A meeting is scheduled for next Wednesday to discuss initial module ideas focusing on the 60-day period following that date, and the Friday meeting was canceled due to Melissa conducting a demo at Christmas (00:03:05).
Sandboxing Solution and Accelerated Development: Gabor Kerekes discussed their work on a sandboxing solution, noting that the sandboxing landscape has recently expanded significantly, which is relevant for accelerating development. They settled on a solution for Mac OS that significantly reduces supervision needs, even though it is not as secure as they would prefer (00:04:16). Gabor Kerekes will share the configuration with the team (00:06:01).
Demonstration of Mycelium Prototype: Gabor Kerekes presented a prototype for a fully functional but limited backend built in a sandbox, which processes a URL and integrates it with existing information about the user. This experiment was designed to prototype the mechanism, validate technology choices, and demonstrate how the system understands and weaves together conceptual threads in the user's daily life, such as their work on the "cognitive exoskeleton" (00:06:01). The prototype successfully attached a new bookmark to the concept of building a cognitive exoskeleton and interpreted its importance (00:10:11).
Current Prototyping Approach and Focus: Amir Houieh plans to continue prototyping their scenario use case primarily at the UI level. Gabor Kerekes also expressed an interest in prototyping new ideas spawned by the backend demo solely on the UI level (00:12:25) (00:18:54). The team agreed that overlapping, experimental code is acceptable and that the current work, including the backend code developed by Gabor Kerekes, is "throwaway code" intended for validating ideas (00:14:46).
Amir Houieh's Work on "Brain Nexus": Amir Houieh reported on their analysis of the Mycelium codebase using an AI model, which extracted 12 use cases and user flows and determined that their "brain nexus" implementation could cover 70% of the scenarios. They identified missing proactivity features and created specifications for necessary adjustments, which they plan to implement today, along with testing the 12 use cases powered by the brain on top of Mycelium (00:18:54). Amir Houieh also plans to quickly sketch a UI-driven use case involving Mycelium assisting with drafting an email (00:20:13).
Discussion on Development Approach: Gabor Kerekes shared an observation about the importance of organic exploration over narrow, top-down objectives to achieve truly novel ideas, citing a book called "Why Greatness Cannot Be Planned" (00:21:34). This led to a discussion where Amir Houieh confirmed that the core concept of Mycelium is aligned with everyone's interests, and for them, the internal mechanisms of how the system learns (the brain) are the most motivating area of focus (00:23:35).
Integrating the Brain Nexus into Experiments: Gabor Kerekes suggested that Amir Houieh should hook the "brain nexus" up to a specific use case, such as the email functionality, to anchor it in a concrete experiment with a UI for validation (00:25:00). Amir Houieh agreed that this approach would be a good validation of the brain's architecture and intends to implement only cosmetic adjustments before prototyping the Mycelium use cases (00:26:19). Amir Houieh emphasized that the brain is a personal hobby project, which they would like to put to the test as an experiment (00:27:28).
Clarifying UI-Driven Use Case Prototyping: Amir Houieh clarified that their practical use case involves a UI-driven exploration of how Mycelium could exist at the OS level and provide relevant context when interacting with applications like email (00:28:52). They described their design approach as 'faking' data and scenarios to quickly generate different sketches and gain a clearer idea of the UI before worrying about real data or complex backends (00:30:59).
Technology Validation and Offline Support: Gabor Kerekes mentioned they are also validating technology choices that will allow the system to have first-class offline support, which is a priority for saving notes and reading articles without back-end reliance. They agreed that their different approaches to development (mockups vs. dynamic prototypes) are both working for the project (00:34:59).
Connecting Website to Domain and Task Allocation: Amir Houieh confirmed that they will connect the website to the domain today (00:36:29). Regarding the visualization work for Cibil, Gabor Kerekes suggested they each proceed with their own initial explorations, which they will then converge on in a meeting. Amir Houieh expressed a willingness to help as a developer but can provide input on design if needed (00:37:25).
Review of Safety Architecture and Tier Classification: Noémi Biró shared visualizations and a deep dive into the safety documents, noting that Melissa defined a six-layer architecture for message processing (00:38:36). This architecture includes a tier classifier that categorizes messages into five tiers (e.g., low risk, high distress, crisis), which Noémi Biró redefined as taxonomy for better clarity. Noémi Biró suggested that a session manager, which considers the user's current tier and associated rules, should be one of the first features implemented (00:40:04) (00:42:28).
Session Manager Focus and Strategic Priority: Noémi Biró believes that configuring the session manager to focus on user retention would be more beneficial initially than addressing potential addiction, though ideas for retention and security overlap (00:40:04). Amir Houieh agreed that the safety architecture work should strategically remain a background task since the chat function is not the main focus. Amir Houieh plans to review the safety regulation document shared by Melissa and provide comments on their free time (00:45:06).
Planning for Cibil Module Brainstorming: Noémi Biró and Amir Houieh agreed to meet on Friday, after the daily meeting, for a working session to brainstorm and review the Cibil module explorations, ensuring they have multiple ideas prepared by Wednesday's meeting. Noémi Biró confirmed they would focus on Mycelium today (00:46:38).
Suggested next steps
Amir Houieh will review and measure the website's back button functionality on the phone and connect the website to the domain today.
Amir Houieh will go through the Google Docs document that Melissa shared and make relevant comments sometime this week.
Gabor Kerekes will share the sandboxing configuration with the group.
Noémi Biró and Amir Houieh will meet on Friday after the daily session for a working session to brainstorm and look at the Cibil exploration.
